RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Planning Commission adopt RESOLUTION NO.
PC-2021-013 finding that the proposed Capital Improvement Project (CIP) budget for
Fiscal Years (FY) 2021-22, 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 is consistent with
the goals, objectives, and policies of the General Plan and Government
Code Section 65103 and recommending adoption by the City Council.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

A CIP budget is a planning tool for the expenditure of resources for public infrastructure.
It is a short-range, two-year plan, which identifies capital projects and related special
studies, provides a planning schedule, and identifies options for financing the program.

The City’s CIP budget document identifies the recommended allocation of the City’s
limited resources for capital projects for FYs 2022 through 2026.

BACKGROUND

Staff is proposing a budget for CIP for FY’s 2021-22, 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and
2025-26. The City Council is required to adopt a balanced budget by June 30th and,
therefore, consistency with the General Plan must be completed prior to budget adoption.

Section 65103 of the Government Code requires that each City annually review the CIP
for consistency with the General Plan. The purpose of the consistency review is to ensure
that capital improvement projects are not placed in locations that are designated for other
purposes under the General Plan and to ensure that the budgeted improvements are
consistent with the goals, objectives, and policies of the General Plan.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

Review of the FY 2021-22 and FY 2022-23 biennial CIP budget is not an approval of the
individual actions within the budget; it is only a determination that the budget is in
conformance with the City’s General Plan. The individual actions described in the
FY 2021-22 and FY 2022-23 biennial CIP budget are speculative and the determination
of conformance does not commit funding to any specific project. Therefore, the proposed
action is not a “Project” as defined in Section 15378(b)(4) of the CEQA Guidelines, which
states that: Project does not include: The creation of government funding mechanisms
or other government fiscal activities, which do not involve any commitment to any specific
project, which may result in a potentially significant impact on the environment.

Therefore, it has been determined that the finding of conformance with the City’s General
Plan is exempt from the requirements of the CEQA pursuant to the general rule
[Section 15061(b)(3)] of the State CEQA Guidelines which states that CEQA applies only
to projects which have the potential for causing a significant physical effect on the
environment. Where it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the
activity in question may have a significant physical effect on the environment, the activity
is not subject to CEQA.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Planning Commission adopt RESOLUTION NO. PC-2021-008
(ATTACHMENT 1) recommending approval of Zoning Ordinance Amendment
(ZOA) 21-002 and find that the project is not subject to the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA).

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The proposed ZOA would amend Sections 17.16 (Definitions), 17.26.040 (Minor
Modifications to Approved Plans), 17.95.040 (Communication Facilities), 17.95.05
(Wireless Telecommunication Facilities in the Public Right-of-Way) and to add Section
17.95.060 (Emergency Standby Generators) of Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Title 17
Zoning (Zoning Code) to update the standards for the permitting, development, siting,
installation, aesthetics, design, operation and maintenance of wireless
telecommunication facilities and to provide for the installation of Emergency Standby
Generators in compliance with State and Federal requirements.

BACKGROUND

In addition to initialization of the 5G network, the Federal Communications Commission
(FCC) now requires the installation of backup electricity in the form of emergency standby
generators for wireless telecommunication facilities. This has resulted in an increase in
the number of requests to modify existing wireless facilities. The proposed ZOA is
intended to bring the PMC into compliance with State and Federal regulations regarding
wireless telecommunication facilities. The proposed ZOA also provides us with the
opportunity to address requirements for eligible facilities and to take a close look at and

  ANALYSIS

  ZOA’s occur over time in order to improve the quality of life, provide convenience, and to
  remain current with local government best practices. As sections of the Zoning Code have
  been independently amended over time, the document now contains issues of non-
  conformance with State and Federal regulations and requirements, which make it difficult
  for the telecommunications community to find what they are looking for, understand what
  they find and process applications. ZOA 21-002 addresses these issues by revising
  portions of the Zoning Code to create a more user-friendly document that is internally
  consistent, consistent with State and Federal requirements and regulations and
  consistent with the General Plan.

  This amendment aims to address changes primarily resulting from new State and Federal
  regulations and requirements. Additional proposed changes include the addition of
  provisions for emergency standby generators and clarification of the submittal and
  approval process for minor facilities and eligible facilities requests.

  PMC Sections 17.95.040 and 17.95.05 address wireless telecommunication facilities on
  private and public property and provide users with regulations and standards to facilitate
  a variety of communication services. The proposed regulations are intended to serve the
  wireless telecommunication needs of the local population while avoiding impacts resulting
  from the unregulated proliferation of communication facilities. The proposed ZOA would
  add definitions for industry terminology consistent with State and Federal regulations,
  simplify the process of considering minor modifications, clarify eligible facilities requests
  and add provisions for the installation of emergency standby generators. Failure to
  amend the code for conformance with State and Federal regulations could lead to
  negative consequences for non-compliance.
